name: Tension and Trauma Releasing Exercises

card.summary: A set of leg and core exercises, devised by David Berceli, that bring on body tremors; practitioners use them to release tension, ease stress and sleep and train better, which can show in how they look.
card.note: Not a substitute for professional care; those with trauma histories are advised to learn it with a certified provider.

quick.overview:
Tension and Trauma Releasing Exercises (TRE) are a sequence of simple exercises that tire the legs and core to trigger neurogenic tremors, a shaking the method describes as the body discharging stress. Practitioners report calmer nerves, better sleep, less muscle tension and more energy.

For appearance, the link is through stress, sleep and tension: a relaxed face and posture and better recovery to train. This is a claimed chain. One small randomized trial in restless legs syndrome found TRE and a discussion group improved to a similar degree.
quick.how: People learn the exercises, ideally with a certified TRE provider, then practise them as short self-directed sessions that induce tremors and let them stop on their own.
quick.risks: Berceli-linked sources advise those with complex trauma, medical conditions or psychological vulnerabilities to work with a certified provider.[1] In the restless legs trial one TRE participant had emotional discomfort, which was managed.[2]

lead: Tension and Trauma Releasing Exercises (TRE) is a body-based technique developed by David Berceli, who describes it as activating a natural tremor reflex to release muscular patterns of stress and trauma.[1] Practitioners say it reduces anxiety, improves sleep, eases pain and raises energy.[1]

Berceli says he developed the method after more than two decades working in conflict zones including Lebanon and African countries, where he observed children trembling during air raids while adults suppressed the reflex, and animals shaking after escaping predators.[1]

For looks, proponents point to relaxation and recovery: less chronic tension, better sleep and more training capacity. One small randomized trial in restless legs syndrome found no difference between TRE and a discussion group.[2]

chain: Reported lower tension and better sleep
More relaxed posture and better recovery
angle.text: People use TRE to relax chronically tense muscles and manage stress, which they associate with better sleep, recovery and a more relaxed look.

paras: TRE uses a series of gentle exercises that fatigue leg and core muscles to start involuntary tremors that begin in the pelvis and spread through the body.[1] The method treats chronic tension, including in the psoas, as stored protective contraction.[1]
Berceli developed TRE through fieldwork in conflict areas including Lebanon, Sudan, Uganda and Kenya.[1] It is promoted by a nonprofit, TRE For All, through certified providers.[1]

An exploratory randomized trial in Victoria, Australia enrolled 18 adults with restless legs syndrome, comparing a 5-week TRE programme with a discussion group. At 6 weeks there were no significant between-group differences and both groups improved; the authors noted the small sample and possible effects of regression to the mean and group support.[2] Larger trials in other conditions are registered or proposed.
Providers advise that TRE is not a substitute for medical or psychological treatment and recommend certified guidance for people with complex trauma.[1]
